explanation: Total fuel flow is n T ce/1000 in kg/s. Multiply by duration×60 seconds to obtain 1351.7 kg. Multiply total thrust by the engine count, not specific consumption separately.

option_explanations.1.3517e+06 kg: Fails to convert grams to kilograms.
option_explanations.1351.7 kg: Correct. Total fuel flow is n T ce/1000 in kg/s. Multiply by duration×60 seconds to obtain 1351.7 kg. Multiply total thrust by the engine count, not specific consumption separately.

steps: Total fuel flow is n T ce/1000 in kg/s.
Multiply by duration×60 seconds to obtain 1351.7 kg.
Multiply total thrust by the engine count, not specific consumption separately..

subtopic: The same force passes through both segments.
stem: Two axial segments in series carry F=10400 N. Segment 1 has L=0.76 m, E=7e+10 Pa, A=0.000132 m²; segment 2 has L=0.98 m, E=1.1e+11 Pa, A=0.0001 m². Joints are rigid and both segments are elastic. What is the total extension in mm? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The same force passes through both segments. Add extensions: delta=F L1/(E1 A1)+F L2/(E2 A2)=0.001782 m. Convert metres to millimetres.

option_explanations.1.782 mm: Correct. The same force passes through both segments. Add extensions: delta=F L1/(E1 A1)+F L2/(E2 A2)=0.001782 m. Convert metres to millimetres.
option_explanations.3.5639 mm: Doubles the required sum of extensions.
option_explanations.1.1143 mm: Combines areas as if the segments acted in parallel and uses only E1.
option_explanations.0.89098 mm: Halves the required sum of extensions.

steps: The same force passes through both segments.
Add extensions: delta=F L1/(E1 A1)+F L2/(E2 A2)=0.001782 m.

stem: An ideal column with E=7e+10 Pa, I=2.1e-08 m⁴ and effective-length factor K=0.75 carries F=8000 N. Require Euler critical load to be at least 1.46 times F. What maximum physical length L is permitted? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Euler gives Pcrit=pi²EI/(KL)². Set Pcrit=sf F and solve L_max=pi sqrt[EI/(sf F)]/K=1.486 m.

option_explanations.0.83589 m: Multiplies by K instead of dividing when recovering physical length.
option_explanations.1.1145 m: Returns effective length KL instead of physical length.
option_explanations.1.486 m: Correct. Euler gives Pcrit=pi²EI/(KL)². Set Pcrit=sf F and solve L_max=pi sqrt[EI/(sf F)]/K=1.486 m.

steps: Set Pcrit=sf F and solve L_max=pi sqrt[EI/(sf F)]/K=1.486 m..

stem: The required critical-load gain of a column is 2. Changes give E2/E1=1.09, I2/I1=1.4 and K2/K1=0.94. According to Euler, what is the maximum L2/L1? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Compare critical loads: gain=er×ir/(kr²×lr²). Solve lr_max=sqrt[er×ir/(gain×kr²)]=0.92925.

option_explanations.0.92925: Correct. Compare critical loads: gain=er×ir/(kr²×lr²). Solve lr_max=sqrt[er×ir/(gain×kr²)]=0.92925.
option_explanations.0.8117: Fails to take the square root and treats K linearly.

stem: A rectangular cantilever has E=7e+10 Pa, length 1.28 m, width b=0.039 m and transverse tip load F=290 N. Maximum deflection is 0.0044 m. With I=bh³/12 and y=FL³/(3EI), what minimum section height h is required in mm? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Substitute I into deflection: y=4FL³/(Ebh³). Solve h=[4FL³/(Eb y_lim)]^(1/3)=0.058725 m, then convert to mm.

option_explanations.29.363 mm: Halves the required section height, increasing deflection eightfold.
option_explanations.117.45 mm: Doubles the required height rather than solving the cubic equation.
option_explanations.101.71 mm: Applies an unwarranted square-root-of-three factor to the height.
option_explanations.58.725 mm: Correct. Substitute I into deflection: y=4FL³/(Ebh³). Solve h=[4FL³/(Eb y_lim)]^(1/3)=0.058725 m, then convert to mm.

steps: Solve h=[4FL³/(Eb y_lim)]^(1/3)=0.058725 m, then convert to mm..

stem: A material has E=6.9e+10 Pa and yield stress 2.4e+08 Pa. Allowable stress is yield stress divided by safety factor 1.49. What is the maximum allowable axial strain, as a percentage, in linear elasticity? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Allowable stress is sigma_y/sf. Hooke law gives epsilon_adm=sigma_y/(sf E)=0.0023344. Multiply by 100 for the percentage.

option_explanations.0.0023344 %: Reports dimensionless strain without converting to percent.
option_explanations.0.51826 %: Multiplies yield stress by the safety factor instead of dividing.
option_explanations.0.23344 %: Correct. Allowable stress is sigma_y/sf. Hooke law gives epsilon_adm=sigma_y/(sf E)=0.0023344. Multiply by 100 for the percentage.

stem: A bar with E=7e+10 Pa and length 1.26 m carries tensile load 21000 N. Maximum extension is 0.00081 m. In linear axial elasticity, what minimum area is needed in mm²? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Use delta=FL/(EA). Enforcing the extension limit gives A_min=FL/(E delta_lim)=0.00046667 m². Multiply by 10^6 to express area in mm².

option_explanations.588 mm²: Counts the bar length twice in the area requirement.
option_explanations.370.37 mm²: Omits the bar length in the area requirement.
option_explanations.466.67 mm²: Correct. Use delta=FL/(EA). Enforcing the extension limit gives A_min=FL/(E delta_lim)=0.00046667 m². Multiply by 10^6 to express area in mm².
option_explanations.0.46667 mm²: Uses an incorrect area conversion between m² and mm².

steps: Enforcing the extension limit gives A_min=FL/(E delta_lim)=0.00046667 m².
Multiply by 10^6 to express area in mm²..

stem: For two cantilevers with tip point loads, F2/F1=1.14, L2/L1=1.08, E2/E1=0.95 and I2/I1=1.48. What is the tip-deflection ratio y2/y1? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Use y=FL³/(3EI). Therefore y2/y1=fr×lr³/(er×ir)=1.0214. Length enters cubically.

option_explanations.0.87568: Uses a linear rather than cubic length effect.
option_explanations.0.94573: Uses a squared rather than cubic length effect.
option_explanations.1.0214: Correct. Use y=FL³/(3EI). Therefore y2/y1=fr×lr³/(er×ir)=1.0214. Length enters cubically.

stem: Level flight has m=6800 kg, rho=0.88 kg/m³, V=111 m/s and S=38 m². The wing follows CL=0.176+5.38 alpha, with alpha in radians. With g=9.81 m/s², what angle of attack is needed in degrees within the linear regime? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Calculate equilibrium CL=2mg/(rho V²S)=0.32381. Invert the lift curve: alpha=(CL-CL0)/a=0.027475 rad. Convert radians to degrees.

option_explanations.1.5742 °: Correct. Calculate equilibrium CL=2mg/(rho V²S)=0.32381. Invert the lift curve: alpha=(CL-CL0)/a=0.027475 rad. Convert radians to degrees.
option_explanations.15.443 °: Multiplies the angle by g after weight has already been included.
option_explanations.3.4485 °: Ignores the nonzero lift coefficient at zero angle.

steps: Invert the lift curve: alpha=(CL-CL0)/a=0.027475 rad.

stem: An airfoil has xac/c=0.25 and constant cm_ac=-0.049. Initially cl=0.47. The lift slope is 5.5 per radian and angle of attack increases by 0.029671 rad. With xcp/c=xac/c-cm_ac/cl, find the centre-of-pressure shift in percent chord; positive is aft. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Update cl2=cl1+5.5 delta_alpha=0.63319. Calculate xcp1/c=0.35426 and xcp2/c=0.32739. The shift is 100(xcp2-xcp1)=-2.6869% chord; a negative sign means forward.

option_explanations.2.6869 % chord: Reverses the sign of the centre-of-pressure displacement.
option_explanations.7.7386 % chord: Reports final displacement from the aerodynamic centre instead of the change.
option_explanations.16.319 % chord: Uses lift-coefficient increment as a positional shift.
option_explanations.-2.6869 % chord: Correct. Update cl2=cl1+5.5 delta_alpha=0.63319. Calculate xcp1/c=0.35426 and xcp2/c=0.32739. The shift is 100(xcp2-xcp1)=-2.6869% chord; a negative sign means forward.

steps: The shift is 100(xcp2-xcp1)=-2.6869% chord; a negative sign means forward..

stem: An aircraft keeps weight, area and polar CD=0.022+0.05 CL². Initially CL1=0.65. It changes to rho2/rho1=0.8, V2/V1=1.13. What is the signed percentage change in L/D, defined as 100(E2/E1-1)? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Recover CL2=CL1/(rhor×vr²)=0.63631. Evaluate E1=15.072 and E2=15.063 using CL/CD. The relative percentage change is -0.065828%.

option_explanations.-0.065828 %: Correct. Recover CL2=CL1/(rhor×vr²)=0.63631. Evaluate E1=15.072 and E2=15.063 using CL/CD. The relative percentage change is -0.065828%.
option_explanations.-0.99219 %: Uses an absolute efficiency difference rather than relative change.
option_explanations.-2.1067 %: Uses the lift-coefficient change as the efficiency change.

steps: Evaluate E1=15.072 and E2=15.063 using CL/CD.

stem: An aircraft maintains mass and wing area in two level flights. Initial CL=0.68; then rho2/rho1=0.864 and V2/V1=1.1. What CL is required in the second condition? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Equal lift requires rr×vr²×CL2/CL1=1. Thus CL2=CL1/(rr×vr²)=0.65044.

option_explanations.0.7109: Multiplies CL by the dynamic-pressure ratio rather than dividing.
option_explanations.0.65044: Correct. Equal lift requires rr×vr²×CL2/CL1=1. Thus CL2=CL1/(rr×vr²)=0.65044.
option_explanations.0.71549: Uses speed linearly rather than squared.

stem: A trapezoidal wing has area 44 m², aspect ratio 7.5 and taper ratio lambda=0.44. With AR=b²/S and S=b(cr+ct)/2, what root chord cr is needed? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Find span b=sqrt(AR S)=18.166 m. With ct=lambda cr, root chord is cr=2S/[b(1+lambda)]=3.3641 m.

option_explanations.8.6504 m: Uses a chord difference instead of the chord sum in trapezoidal area.
option_explanations.2.4221 m: Returns mean geometric chord instead of root chord.
option_explanations.1.4802 m: Returns tip chord instead of root chord.
option_explanations.3.3641 m: Correct. Find span b=sqrt(AR S)=18.166 m. With ct=lambda cr, root chord is cr=2S/[b(1+lambda)]=3.3641 m.

steps: With ct=lambda cr, root chord is cr=2S/[b(1+lambda)]=3.3641 m..

subtopic: Calculate MGC=2.828 m and MAC=3.0011 m separately.
stem: For a trapezoidal wing, root chord is 4.04 m and taper ratio is 0.4. Find mean aerodynamic chord minus mean geometric chord. Use MGC=cr(1+lambda)/2 and MAC=(2cr/3)(1+lambda+lambda²)/(1+lambda). Choose the closest value.
explanation: Calculate MGC=2.828 m and MAC=3.0011 m separately. Subtract MGC from MAC to obtain 0.17314 m.

option_explanations.0.17314 m: Correct. Calculate MGC=2.828 m and MAC=3.0011 m separately. Subtract MGC from MAC to obtain 0.17314 m.
option_explanations.3.0011 m: Returns MAC alone instead of the difference.
option_explanations.2.828 m: Returns MGC alone instead of the difference.

steps: Calculate MGC=2.828 m and MAC=3.0011 m separately.
Subtract MGC from MAC to obtain 0.17314 m..

stem: A strictly trapezoidal wing has span 18.4 m, root chord 3.3 m and area 40 m². What is taper ratio lambda? Use S=b(cr+ct)/2. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Recover tip chord ct=2S/b-cr=1.0478 m. Taper ratio is lambda=ct/cr=0.31752.

option_explanations.0.31752: Correct. Recover tip chord ct=2S/b-cr=1.0478 m. Taper ratio is lambda=ct/cr=0.31752.
option_explanations.1.0478: Returns dimensional tip chord instead of the chord ratio.
option_explanations.0.65876: Treats mean geometric chord as tip chord.

subtopic: Stall speed squared is inversely proportional to S CLmax.
stem: A high-lift device reduces true stall speed from 232 to 178 km/h at the same weight and density. Effective area increases by factor 1.08. CLmax is referenced to each configuration's own area. What CLmax2/CLmax1 is required? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Stall speed squared is inversely proportional to S CLmax. Therefore CLmax2/CLmax1=(Vs1/Vs2)²/sr=1.5729.

option_explanations.1.6988: Attributes the entire improvement to CLmax and omits the area increase.
option_explanations.1.5729: Correct. Stall speed squared is inversely proportional to S CLmax. Therefore CLmax2/CLmax1=(Vs1/Vs2)²/sr=1.5729.
option_explanations.0.63575: Reverses the speed ratio and applies the area change in the wrong direction.
option_explanations.1.2068: Uses a linear speed ratio instead of its square.

steps: Stall speed squared is inversely proportional to S CLmax.

subtopic: The last two digits give thickness/chord=14%.
stem: A NACA 4514 airfoil must have dimensional maximum thickness 0.284 m. From its four-digit designation, how far from the leading edge is the point of maximum camber? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The last two digits give thickness/chord=14%. Thus chord=2.0286 m. The second digit gives x/c=5/10, so maximum camber is at x=1.0143 m.

option_explanations.0.10143 m: Interprets the second digit in hundredths rather than tenths of chord.
option_explanations.0.081143 m: Uses the camber magnitude digit as a position.
option_explanations.0.284 m: Returns maximum thickness rather than maximum-camber position.
option_explanations.1.0143 m: Correct. The last two digits give thickness/chord=14%. Thus chord=2.0286 m. The second digit gives x/c=5/10, so maximum camber is at x=1.0143 m.

steps: The last two digits give thickness/chord=14%.
The second digit gives x/c=5/10, so maximum camber is at x=1.0143 m..

subtopic: Set rho2 V2 c2/mu2=rho1 V1 c1/mu1.
stem: A wind-tunnel model must match the Reynolds number of a wing of chord 1.56 m. Ratios in the tunnel are rho2/rho1=0.75, V2/V1=1.19, mu2/mu1=1.08. What model chord is required? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Set rho2 V2 c2/mu2=rho1 V1 c1/mu1. Solve c2=c1×mur/(rhor×vr)=1.8877 m.

option_explanations.1.8877 m: Correct. Set rho2 V2 c2/mu2=rho1 V1 c1/mu1. Solve c2=c1×mur/(rhor×vr)=1.8877 m.
option_explanations.1.2892 m: Inverts the required density, speed and viscosity correction.

steps: Set rho2 V2 c2/mu2=rho1 V1 c1/mu1.

stem: A wing follows CD=CD0+CL²/(pi e AR), with CD0=0.02, e=0.8 and AR=7.6. What is the maximum L/D allowed by this model? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Set k=1/(pi e AR)=0.052354. At CL*=sqrt(CD0/k), induced and zero-lift drag are equal. Therefore Emax=1/[2sqrt(CD0 k)]=15.452.

option_explanations.30.904: Omits the factor 2 in the maximum-efficiency formula.
option_explanations.477.52: Omits the square root in the maximum-efficiency formula.
option_explanations.15.452: Correct. Set k=1/(pi e AR)=0.052354. At CL*=sqrt(CD0/k), induced and zero-lift drag are equal. Therefore Emax=1/[2sqrt(CD0 k)]=15.452.
option_explanations.0.61808: Returns the optimum CL rather than maximum L/D.

steps: At CL*=sqrt(CD0/k), induced and zero-lift drag are equal.

stem: Horizontal flight has weight 98100 N, rho=0.94 kg/m³, V=116 m/s and S=42 m². The polar is CD=0.023+0.045 CL². What total thrust in kN balances drag? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Enforce L=W to obtain CL=W/(qS)=0.36932. Evaluate CD=0.029138, then D=qS CD=7739.7 N. Required thrust equals drag; divide by 1000 for kN.

option_explanations.0.78896 kN: Divides force by g, confusing force and mass.
option_explanations.6.1093 kN: Includes only zero-lift drag and omits induced drag.
option_explanations.7.7397 kN: Correct. Enforce L=W to obtain CL=W/(qS)=0.36932. Evaluate CD=0.029138, then D=qS CD=7739.7 N. Required thrust equals drag; divide by 1000 for kN.

steps: Evaluate CD=0.029138, then D=qS CD=7739.7 N.
Required thrust equals drag; divide by 1000 for kN..

stem: A sensor must maintain dynamic pressure q=3800 Pa at static pressure p=68000 Pa and T=259 K. With ideal air R=287 J/(kg K), what true airspeed is required in km/h? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Calculate rho=p/(RT)=0.9148 kg/m³. Invert q=rho V²/2: V=sqrt(2q/rho)=91.147 m/s. Multiply by 3.6 for km/h.

option_explanations.232.02 km/h: Omits the factor 2 when solving for speed.
option_explanations.328.13 km/h: Correct. Calculate rho=p/(RT)=0.9148 kg/m³. Invert q=rho V²/2: V=sqrt(2q/rho)=91.147 m/s. Multiply by 3.6 for km/h.

stem: Initial minimum-drag speed is 133 m/s. Wing area is fixed, but W2/W1=0.874, rho2/rho1=0.8, k2/k1=1.15, CD02/CD01=0.956. For a parabolic polar in level flight, what is the new minimum-drag speed? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Use Vmd=sqrt[2W/(rho S)](k/CD0)^(1/4). The speed ratio is sqrt(mr/rr)(kr/cdr)^(1/4)=1.0946; multiply by initial speed.

option_explanations.174.79 m/s: Treats all parameter ratios linearly rather than with square and fourth roots.
option_explanations.145.59 m/s: Correct. Use Vmd=sqrt[2W/(rho S)](k/CD0)^(1/4). The speed ratio is sqrt(mr/rr)(kr/cdr)^(1/4)=1.0946; multiply by initial speed.

steps: The speed ratio is sqrt(mr/rr)(kr/cdr)^(1/4)=1.0946; multiply by initial speed..

explanation: From Vs=sqrt(2mg/(rho S CLmax)), Vs2=Vs1 sqrt[massratio/(rhoratio×clratio)]=176.15 km/h.

stem: An aircraft of mass 39000 kg flies level with L/D=14.6, using 2 identical engines, each with ce=14.6 g/(kN s). With g=9.81 m/s² and constant conditions, what total fuel mass is burned in 39 min? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Total thrust equals W/E=26205 N. Convert ce to kg/(N s); total fuel flow is ce×T=0.38259 kg/s. Multiply by elapsed seconds to obtain 895.26 kg.

option_explanations.1790.5 kg: Multiplies by engine count after already using total aircraft thrust.
option_explanations.14.921 kg: Treats the duration in minutes as seconds.

option_explanations.895.26 kg: Correct. Total thrust equals W/E=26205 N. Convert ce to kg/(N s); total fuel flow is ce×T=0.38259 kg/s. Multiply by elapsed seconds to obtain 895.26 kg.

stem: An engine produces T=8300 N with mass flow 34 kg/s, V0=170 m/s, exit area 0.204 m² and pe-pamb=10000 Pa. Using T=m_dot(Ve-V0)+Ae(pe-pamb), what exit velocity Ve is required? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Pressure thrust is Ae delta_p. Subtract it from total thrust, divide the momentum contribution by flow and add inlet velocity: Ve=V0+(T-Ae delta_p)/m_dot=354.12 m/s.

option_explanations.184.12 m/s: Returns only the velocity increase and omits inlet speed.
option_explanations.474.12 m/s: Adds pressure thrust instead of subtracting it.
option_explanations.354.12 m/s: Correct. Pressure thrust is Ae delta_p. Subtract it from total thrust, divide the momentum contribution by flow and add inlet velocity: Ve=V0+(T-Ae delta_p)/m_dot=354.12 m/s.

steps: Subtract it from total thrust, divide the momentum contribution by flow and add inlet velocity: Ve=V0+(T-Ae delta_p)/m_dot=354.12 m/s..

stem: An ideal propulsor ingests 71 kg/s at V0=133 m/s and produces 5900 N. Neglect pressure thrust and added fuel mass. What kinetic power in kW is transferred to the flow? Use T=m_dot(Ve-V0). Choose the closest value.
explanation: First Ve=V0+T/m_dot=216.1 m/s. Flow kinetic-power increase is m_dot(Ve²-V0²)/2=1.0298e+06 W. Divide by 1000 for kW.

option_explanations.1029.8 kW: Correct. First Ve=V0+T/m_dot=216.1 m/s. Flow kinetic-power increase is m_dot(Ve²-V0²)/2=1.0298e+06 W. Divide by 1000 for kW.
option_explanations.784.7 kW: Returns useful propulsive power TV0 rather than flow kinetic power.
option_explanations.2059.7 kW: Omits the factor 1/2 in kinetic power.
option_explanations.245.14 kW: Squares only the velocity increment and omits the cross term.

steps: Flow kinetic-power increase is m_dot(Ve²-V0²)/2=1.0298e+06 W.

subtopic: Total propellant flow is T/(Isp g0).
stem: A rocket maintains T=13600 N and Isp=259 s for 38 s. Oxidizer/fuel mass ratio is 2.6; g0=9.81 m/s². What fuel mass alone, excluding oxidizer, is consumed? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Total propellant flow is T/(Isp g0). Total propellant mass is 203.4 kg. Since oxidizer mass=ratio×fuel mass, fuel=propellant/(1+ratio)=56.5 kg.

option_explanations.78.231 kg: Divides by the oxidizer/fuel ratio without including fuel itself in total mass.
option_explanations.56.5 kg: Correct. Total propellant flow is T/(Isp g0). Total propellant mass is 203.4 kg. Since oxidizer mass=ratio×fuel mass, fuel=propellant/(1+ratio)=56.5 kg.
option_explanations.146.9 kg: Returns oxidizer mass instead of fuel mass.

steps: Total propellant flow is T/(Isp g0).
Since oxidizer mass=ratio×fuel mass, fuel=propellant/(1+ratio)=56.5 kg..

subtopic: Bypass mass flow is B times core flow.
stem: An ideal turbofan has core flow 22 kg/s, bypass ratio 4.5, inlet speed 170 m/s, core exit speed 516 m/s and bypass exit speed 278 m/s. Neglect pressure terms and added fuel mass. What total thrust is produced in kN? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Bypass mass flow is B times core flow. Add stream momentum changes: T=m_core(Vec-V0)+B m_core(Veb-V0)=18304 N. Convert N to kN.

option_explanations.41.866 kN: Applies the core velocity increase to both streams.
option_explanations.18.304 kN: Correct. Bypass mass flow is B times core flow. Add stream momentum changes: T=m_core(Vec-V0)+B m_core(Veb-V0)=18304 N. Convert N to kN.

steps: Bypass mass flow is B times core flow.
Add stream momentum changes: T=m_core(Vec-V0)+B m_core(Veb-V0)=18304 N.

subtopic: Invert efficiency to obtain Ve=V0(2/eta_p-1)=245.06 m/s.
stem: An ideal jet must produce 6100 N at V0=160 m/s with propulsive efficiency eta_p=0.79. Neglect pressure thrust. Use eta_p=2/(1+Ve/V0) and T=m_dot(Ve-V0). What air mass flow is required? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Invert efficiency to obtain Ve=V0(2/eta_p-1)=245.06 m/s. Then m_dot=T/(Ve-V0)=71.711 kg/s.

option_explanations.71.711 kg/s: Correct. Invert efficiency to obtain Ve=V0(2/eta_p-1)=245.06 m/s. Then m_dot=T/(Ve-V0)=71.711 kg/s.
option_explanations.38.125 kg/s: Divides thrust by inlet speed instead of the velocity increase.
option_explanations.56.652 kg/s: Applies efficiency a second time after solving the velocity change.
option_explanations.24.892 kg/s: Divides thrust by exit speed instead of the velocity increase.

steps: Invert efficiency to obtain Ve=V0(2/eta_p-1)=245.06 m/s.

stem: An ideal probe measures total temperature Tt=292 K at flow speed V=217 m/s. Air has cp=1004.5 J/(kg K), gamma=1.4 and R=287 J/(kg K). For adiabatic deceleration, what is the Mach number? Recover static temperature first. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Recover T=Tt-V²/(2cp)=268.56 K. Calculate a=sqrt(gamma RT), then M=V/a=0.66059.

option_explanations.0.63824: Uses a fixed sound speed of 340 m/s.
option_explanations.0.66059: Correct. Recover T=Tt-V²/(2cp)=268.56 K. Calculate a=sqrt(gamma RT), then M=V/a=0.66059.
option_explanations.1.0873: Returns a temperature ratio rather than Mach.

lesson_steps.stem: At 9.25 km, pressure is 29.61 kPa. At 13 km, pressure is 16.50 kPa. What is the ratio of the second pressure to the first?

stem: An ideal 28 V, 40 Ah battery supplies a constant 560 W load. What is its ideal endurance?
explanation: Energy is 28 × 40 = 1120 Wh, so ideal duration is 1120/560 = 2 h; usable duration can be lower.

subtopic: Ground speeds are V-w and V+w.

explanation: Ground speeds are V-w and V+w. Add the two times: t=d/(V-w)+d/(V+w)=3.1431 h. Opposite winds do not cancel travel-time penalties.

lesson_steps.stem: The outbound leg is 380 km at a ground speed of 217 km/h. How long does it take?
lesson_steps.explanation: Outbound time is distance divided by ground speed: 380 ÷ 217 = 1.7512 h.

lesson_steps.stem: The outbound leg takes 1.7512 h and the return takes 1.3919 h. What is the total flight time?
lesson_steps.explanation: Add the two stated times: 1.7512 + 1.3919 = 3.1431 h.

explanation: Final mass includes reserve: mf=OEM+payload+reserve=43860 kg. Invert Breguet to obtain mi=mf exp[Rgce/(VE)]=48126 kg. Loaded fuel=mi-OEM-payload=6825.6 kg.

subtopic: Stall speed squared is inversely proportional to S CLmax.

stem: At constant static temperature, an aircraft flies at the maximum Mach number allowed by a leading-edge heating limit. It climbs to air density 20% lower while weight and configuration remain unchanged. The same heating limit applies. What lift-coefficient ratio is required in steady level flight?
explanation: The unchanged static temperature and stagnation-temperature limit give the same limiting Mach number and true airspeed. Lift balance then requires CL2/CL1 = rho1/rho2 = 1/0.80 = 1.25. This combines the heating limit with the density effect rather than treating them independently.

subtopic: Calculate CL=0.42909, drag D=6536.8 N and fuel flow ce D.
stem: A round trip has two legs of 1.6e+05 m each at true airspeed 115 m/s. Estimate cruise at constant mean weight 82000 N, rho=0.85 kg/m³, area 34 m², polar CD=0.025+0.05 CL² and ce=1.6e-05 kg/(N s). Available fuel for these two legs is 343.42 kg, with no other phases or reserves. Steady wind is a headwind outbound and tailwind inbound. What maximum wind magnitude w<V meets the fuel budget? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Calculate CL=0.42909, drag D=6536.8 N and fuel flow ce D. Fuel budget permits tmax=3283.5 s. Since t=d/(V-w)+d/(V+w)=2dV/(V²-w²), solve wmax=sqrt[V²-2dV/tmax]=44.915 m/s.

option_explanations.87.299 m/s: Omits one leg in the round-trip time inversion.
option_explanations.161.69 m/s: Converts the result to km/h while retaining the m/s label.
option_explanations.44.915 m/s: Correct. Calculate CL=0.42909, drag D=6536.8 N and fuel flow ce D. Fuel budget permits tmax=3283.5 s. Since t=d/(V-w)+d/(V+w)=2dV/(V²-w²), solve wmax=sqrt[V²-2dV/tmax]=44.915 m/s.
option_explanations.17.542 m/s: Uses a linear headwind correction instead of adding both leg times.

stem: An ideal jet has OEM=23000 kg, MTOM=53000 kg, maximum landing mass=45000 kg, maximum payload=22000 kg and fuel capacity=15000 kg. It must finish with reserve 2000 kg and cover 3.2e+06 m at V=220 m/s, E=15, ce=1.4e-05 kg/(N s), g=9.81 m/s². There are no other phases. What maximum payload satisfies every limit, including fuel required by the resulting aircraft mass? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Set k=exp[Rgce/(VE)]=1.1425. Final mass=OEM+payload+reserve and initial mass=k×final mass. Loaded fuel=(k-1)(OEM+payload)+k reserve. Derive payload upper bounds from maximum payload, take-off mass, landing mass and tank capacity; their values are 22000, 21391, 20000, 66258. The minimum is 20000 kg.

option_explanations.28000 kg: Subtracts only reserve from the take-off payload allowance, omitting fuel that must be burned to complete the mission.
option_explanations.20000 kg: Correct. Set k=exp[Rgce/(VE)]=1.1425. Final mass=OEM+payload+reserve and initial mass=k×final mass. Loaded fuel=(k-1)(OEM+payload)+k reserve. Derive payload upper bounds from maximum payload, take-off mass, landing mass and tank capacity; their values are 22000, 21391, 20000, 66258. The minimum is 20000 kg.
option_explanations.22000 kg: Omits final fuel reserve from the landing mass balance.
option_explanations.15000 kg: Subtracts full tank fuel from MTOM without coupling required fuel to mission mass.

stem: An ideal jet has OEM=25000 kg, payload=13000 kg, MTOM=56000 kg and fuel capacity=15000 kg. It burns 1800 kg before cruise and must retain 2300 kg after cruise. With V=225 m/s, E=16, ce=1.4e-05 kg/(N s) and g=9.81 m/s², what maximum cruise range remains in km? Enforce both MTOM and tank capacity. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Take-off mass=min(MTOM,OEM+payload+tank capacity)=53000 kg. Cruise initial mass=51200 kg after prior burn; final mass=OEM+payload+reserve=40300 kg. Apply R=VE ln(mi/mf)/(g ce)=6.2749e+06 m and convert to km.

option_explanations.7767.5 km: Uses MTOM as the take-off mass without checking whether the tank can supply that much fuel.
option_explanations.6274.9 km: Correct. Take-off mass=min(MTOM,OEM+payload+tank capacity)=53000 kg. Cruise initial mass=51200 kg after prior burn; final mass=OEM+payload+reserve=40300 kg. Apply R=VE ln(mi/mf)/(g ce)=6.2749e+06 m and convert to km.

option_explanations.7815.3 km: Burns the required reserve during cruise.

With I=bh³/12 and A=bh, what minimum height h is needed in mm? Width may shrink as height grows; there are no other geometric limits. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Eliminate width using b=A/h. Then I=Ah²/12 and y=4FL³/(EA h²). Solve hmin=sqrt[4FL³/(EA y_lim)]=0.082186 m. The corresponding width is b=0.015818 m.

explanation: Stress requires I>=FLh/(2 sigma_allow)=1.4929e-06 m⁴. Deflection requires I>=FL³/(3E y_lim)=4.4539e-06 m⁴. Choose their maximum I=4.4539e-06 m⁴, and express in 10^-6 m⁴.

stem: A finite, unswept subsonic wing has b=18 m, S=39 m², CL0=0.20 and a0=2pi rad⁻¹ for its sections. Use a=a0/[1+a0/(pi AR)]. At W=92000 N, rho=0.82 kg/m³ and TAS=105 m/s, what angle of attack is needed for level flight, assuming attached linear flow? Choose the closest value.
explanation: AR=b²/S=8.3077, hence the finite-wing slope is a=5.0641 rad⁻¹. Level flight requires CL=0.52187. alpha=(CL−CL0)/a=0.063559 rad=3.6417°. A two-dimensional section slope would underpredict the required angle.

option_explanations.3.6417 degrees: Correct. AR=b²/S=8.3077, hence the finite-wing slope is a=5.0641 rad⁻¹. Level flight requires CL=0.52187. alpha=(CL−CL0)/a=0.063559 rad=3.6417°. A two-dimensional section slope would underpredict the required angle.

subtopic: Identify two aerodynamic constants from two measurements
stem: A wing is measured at (CL=0.35, xcp/c=0.34929) and (CL=0.7, xcp/c=0.29214). Assume xcp/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL with constant xac and Cm_ac. From the second state, weight falls to 0.85 of its value while rho, V and S stay fixed in level flight. Predict the new xcp/c by first identifying xac and Cm_ac from the two measurements. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Subtract the two pressure-centre equations: Cm_ac=-0.04, then xac/c=0.235. Constant qS makes CL3=CL2·W3/W2=0.595. Hence xcp3/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL3=0.30223. The aerodynamic centre does not move with consumed fuel in this model.

option_explanations.0.30223: Correct. Subtract the two pressure-centre equations: Cm_ac=-0.04, then xac/c=0.235. Constant qS makes CL3=CL2·W3/W2=0.595. Hence xcp3/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL3=0.30223. The aerodynamic centre does not move with consumed fuel in this model.
option_explanations.0.29214: Keeps the pressure centre fixed although CL has changed.
option_explanations.0.28357: Inverts the weight ratio when updating CL.
option_explanations.0.31723: Assumes exactly quarter-chord instead of using the centre inferred from the measurements.

stem: An initially level aircraft has W=105000 N, rho=0.87 kg/m³, S=40 m² and lift-curve slope a=5.1 rad⁻¹. A vertical gust of 8 m/s adds delta_alpha≈w_g/V, so CL increases linearly. Require load factor n<= 2.1 and M<=0.65 at T=260 K. Use gamma=1.4 and R=287. What is the highest permitted TAS according to these two limits? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The gust lift increment is delta_L=(rho/2)V S a w_g, not proportional to V² after substituting delta_alpha. Thus V_gust=162.69 m/s. The Mach limit is 210.09 m/s; take their minimum: 162.69 m/s. The resulting load factor is 2.1.

option_explanations.162.69 m/s: Correct. The gust lift increment is delta_L=(rho/2)V S a w_g, not proportional to V² after substituting delta_alpha. Thus V_gust=162.69 m/s. The Mach limit is 210.09 m/s; take their minimum: 162.69 m/s. The resulting load factor is 2.1.
option_explanations.210.09 m/s: Uses the looser rather than the tighter of two simultaneous limits.
option_explanations.224.79 m/s: Confuses the incremental load factor n−1 with the total n.
option_explanations.585.7 m/s: Converts the correct speed to km/h although m/s is requested.

stem: A trapezoidal wing has S=38 m², b=16 m and taper ratio 0.45. It uses ONE four-digit NACA profile throughout the span. Structural depth requires maximum section thickness >= 0.29 m at the root and >= 0.19 m at the tip. Which is the thinnest feasible choice: NACA 2412, 2415, 2418 or 2421?

stem: At p=64.6 kPa and T=259 K, an aircraft has W=92000 N, S=34 m² and CLmax=1.91. It must fly at V>=1.3 Vs while q<=6700 Pa and M<=0.612. Use R=287 J/(kg K), gamma=1.4. What is the width of the allowable TRUE-airspeed interval? Choose the closest value.
explanation: rho=p/(RT)=0.86906 kg/m³. The lower bound is 1.3 Vs=74.229 m/s. The upper bound is the smaller of the dynamic-pressure and Mach limits: 124.17 m/s. The interval width is (124.17−74.229)×3.6=179.8 km/h.

stem: Two redundant flight-control computers share one unprotected power feed. What weakness remains?
options: A common power failure can disable both channels
Redundancy guarantees operation after any failure
Only the hydraulic actuators can fail simultaneously
Adding software channels removes all power dependence
explanation: A common cause can defeat redundant channels. Independence of essential supplies matters as well as the number of computers.

stem: A mission has two consecutive cruise legs: 1740 km over ground at TAS=214 m/s into a 24 m/s wind, then 1200 km at TAS=224 m/s with the same tailwind. E1=15.8, ce1=14.24 g/(kN s); E2=16.2, ce2=13.7 g/(kN s). OEM=27200 kg, payload=12500 kg and final reserve=2640 kg. Use g=9.81, separate ideal Breguet legs and no other fuel use. How much fuel must be loaded at the start? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The air distances are Dground·TAS/GS. The two log mass ratios are 0.080969 and 0.040142, which ADD: mi=mf exp(k1+k2). With mf=42340 kg, mi=47791 kg. Loaded fuel=mi−OEM−payload=8091.3 kg, including reserve.

stem: In level flight, groundspeed is 109 m/s with a 15 m/s headwind. Ambient p=60.6 kPa, T=264 K; W=133000 N, S=45 m² and CD=0.026+0.052CL². explanation: TAS=GS+headwind=124 m/s; rho=0.79981. CL=0.48066, drag=10519 N. Momentum supplies 1995.2 N. The remainder requires Ae=[D−m_dot(Ve−V)]/(pe−pamb)=0.67645 m².

stem: An ideal propulsor intercepts m_dot=rho A V, with rho=0.92 kg/m³, A=0.74 m² and V=99 m/s. It transfers 1080 kW of kinetic power to the stream, with no pressure-thrust term. A wing of S=47 m² has CD=0.024+0.05CL². Using Pjet=T·V+T²/(2m_dot) and level flight, what greatest aircraft WEIGHT can its thrust balance? Choose the closest value.
explanation: m_dot=67.399 kg/s. Invert the energy equation: T=m_dot[sqrt(V²+2Pjet/m_dot)−V]=7115.3 N. Parasite drag is 5085.5 N; the remainder can cover induced drag. From D=qSCD0+kW²/(qS), Wmax=92748 N.

subtopic: Relate controlled thrust to changing mass
stem: A vertically climbing rocket starts at 3440 kg and must stop burning at 1960 kg. Isp=270 s. Ignore drag; g=g0=9.81 m/s². The controller adjusts thrust continuously to keep NET upward acceleration=4.9 m/s². Using T=m(g+a) and dm/dt=−T/(Isp g0), how long can the burn last? Here thrust is not constant. Choose the closest value.
explanation: The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=101.29 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

option_explanations.101.29 s: Correct. The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=101.29 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.
option_explanations.77.468 s: Freezes thrust at its initial value and integrates a constant mass flow.
option_explanations.151.88 s: Omits the commanded net acceleration and treats the burn as if T=mg.
option_explanations.304.07 s: Uses net acceleration alone in the thrust law, omitting weight.

stem: An ideal two-stream turbofan has core flow=22 kg/s, V0=184 m/s and core exit speed=426 m/s. Required total thrust is 14500 N and total propulsive efficiency must be at least 0.746. explanation: Tcore=5324 N and Tfan=9176 N. Core kinetic power=1623.8 kW. Fan power=V0 Tfan+Tfan²/(2 B m_core). Applying Ptotal<=Ttotal V0/eta leaves 264.2 kW for the last term, so B>=7.243. This corresponds to fan exit speed 241.59 m/s.

explanation: Transform each test using CL=W/(qS) and CD=D/(qS). Then k=(CD1−CD2)/(CL1²−CL2²)=0.0489, CD0=0.0216. In the new condition CL3=0.45347 and D3=11867 N. Neither measured drag can simply be scaled by V² alone.

stem: At p=65.9 kPa and T=261 K, an aircraft has W=95500 N, S=35 m² and CLmax=1.94. It must fly at V>=1.3 Vs while q<=6800 Pa and M<=0.618. Use R=287 J/(kg K), gamma=1.4. What is the width of the allowable TRUE-airspeed interval? Choose the closest value.
explanation: rho=p/(RT)=0.87976 kg/m³. The lower bound is 1.3 Vs=73.51 m/s. The upper bound is the smaller of the dynamic-pressure and Mach limits: 124.33 m/s. The interval width is (124.33−73.51)×3.6=182.97 km/h.

stem: A runway procedure limits groundspeed on approach to 141 km/h with a steady 19 km/h headwind. Require TAS>=1.3 Vs. At p=74.1 kPa and T=282 K, the aircraft has S=34 m², CLmax=1.975 and a structural mass limit of 4840 kg. Use R=287 and g=9.81. What is the greatest mass meeting both the aerodynamic and structural limits? Choose the closest value.
explanation: A headwind means TAS=GS+headwind, so the largest allowed TAS is 44.444 m/s. rho=0.91556; Vs must be <=TAS/1.3. The resulting aerodynamic mass limit is 3662.5 kg. Intersect it with 4840 kg: 3662.5 kg.

stem: A mission has two consecutive cruise legs: 1810 km over ground at TAS=216 m/s into a 25 m/s wind, then 1250 km at TAS=226 m/s with the same tailwind. E1=15.95, ce1=14.36 g/(kN s); E2=16.3, ce2=13.8 g/(kN s). OEM=27800 kg, payload=12750 kg and final reserve=2710 kg. Use g=9.81, separate ideal Breguet legs and no other fuel use. How much fuel must be loaded at the start? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The air distances are Dground·TAS/GS. The two log mass ratios are 0.083697 and 0.041362, which ADD: mi=mf exp(k1+k2). With mf=43260 kg, mi=49023 kg. Loaded fuel=mi−OEM−payload=8472.9 kg, including reserve.

explanation: TAS=GS+headwind=126.5 m/s; rho=0.81082. CL=0.45908, drag=11030 N. Momentum supplies 2069.2 N. The remainder requires Ae=[D−m_dot(Ve−V)]/(pe−pamb)=0.69459 m².

stem: An ideal propulsor intercepts m_dot=rho A V, with rho=0.93 kg/m³, A=0.76 m² and V=101 m/s. It transfers 1120 kW of kinetic power to the stream, with no pressure-thrust term. A wing of S=48 m² has CD=0.024+0.05CL². Using Pjet=T·V+T²/(2m_dot) and level flight, what greatest aircraft WEIGHT can its thrust balance? Choose the closest value.
explanation: m_dot=71.387 kg/s. Invert the energy equation: T=m_dot[sqrt(V²+2Pjet/m_dot)−V]=7346.4 N. Parasite drag is 5464.5 N; the remainder can cover induced drag. From D=qSCD0+kW²/(qS), Wmax=92574 N.

stem: A vertically climbing rocket starts at 3560 kg and must stop burning at 2040 kg. Isp=275 s. Ignore drag; g=g0=9.81 m/s². The controller adjusts thrust continuously to keep NET upward acceleration=5.1 m/s². Using T=m(g+a) and dm/dt=−T/(Isp g0), how long can the burn last? Here thrust is not constant. Choose the closest value.
explanation: The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=100.75 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

option_explanations.100.75 s: Correct. The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=100.75 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

option_explanations.294.54 s: Uses net acceleration alone in the thrust law, omitting weight.

stem: An ideal two-stream turbofan has core flow=23 kg/s, V0=186 m/s and core exit speed=429 m/s. Required total thrust is 15000 N and total propulsive efficiency must be at least 0.749. explanation: Tcore=5589 N and Tfan=9411 N. Core kinetic power=1718.6 kW. Fan power=V0 Tfan+Tfan²/(2 B m_core). Applying Ptotal<=Ttotal V0/eta leaves 255.9 kW for the last term, so B>=7.5238. This corresponds to fan exit speed 240.38 m/s.

A new engine adds 1800 kg to OEM and gives E2=16.937. Speed, payload, reserve, initial mass and range remain fixed. What maximum signed percentage change in ce preserves range? Negative means consumption must decrease. Use g=9.81 m/s² and model the whole flight as ideal cruise. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Original final mass is 48080 kg and range is 7.5629e+06 m. New final mass is 49880 kg, reducing available fuel. Set ce2_max=V E2 ln(mi/mf2)/(g R1)=1.2634e-05 kg/(N s). The allowable change is 100(ce2_max/ce1-1)=-9.1062%.

option_explanations.-9.1062 %: Correct. Original final mass is 48080 kg and range is 7.5629e+06 m. New final mass is 49880 kg, reducing available fuel. Set ce2_max=V E2 ln(mi/mf2)/(g R1)=1.2634e-05 kg/(N s). The allowable change is 100(ce2_max/ce1-1)=-9.1062%.
option_explanations.9.1062 %: Reverses the sign of the allowable consumption change.
option_explanations.-12.064 %: Uses lost fuel fraction as the consumption change instead of Breguet logarithms.
option_explanations.5.2 %: Credits the efficiency gain but omits the engine mass penalty.

explanation: Compute CL1=0.36305, CD1=0.028063, CL2=0.27741, CD2=0.02554. Efficiencies are E1=CL1/CD1 and E2=CL2/CD2. Breguet gives R2/R1=(V2/V1)(E2/E1)/(ce2/ce1); range change=-9.045%.

subtopic: Convert B test flow to kg/s and divide by test thrust in N: ceB=1.33e-05 kg/(N s).
stem: Engine A has ce=14.8 g/(kN s). Engine B has test fuel flow 3060 L/h, fuel density 0.798 kg/L and test thrust 51 kN. In the mission, required thrust ratio B/A is 0.962; A requires 50 kN. What is the signed percentage change in mission fuel flow B relative to A? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Convert B test flow to kg/s and divide by test thrust in N: ceB=1.33e-05 kg/(N s). Mission fuel-flow ratio=(ceB/(ceA×10^-6))×mission thrust ratio=0.8645. Percentage change=100(ratio-1)=-13.55%. Test thrust establishes ceB; mission thrust determines mission flow.

explanation: Eliminate width using b=A/h. Then I=Ah²/12 and y=4FL³/(EA h²). Solve hmin=sqrt[4FL³/(EA y_lim)]=0.095896 m. The corresponding width is b=0.016059 m.

subtopic: Calculate I, deflection and stress for each candidate.
stem: Compare four rectangular cantilevers under F=310 N, L=1.2 m, E=70 GPa: A 35×45 mm; B 45×50 mm; C 35×60 mm; D 50×55 mm (width×height). Define utilization U=max(y/y_lim,sigma/sigma_lim), where y_lim=0.0072 m and sigma_lim=130 MPa. Use I=bh³/12, y=FL³/(3EI), sigma=FLh/(2I). Which option has the largest simultaneous margin, meaning the smallest U?
explanation: Calculate I, deflection and stress for each candidate. Normalize each by its limit and take the worse utilization. The U values for A, B, C and D are 1.333, 0.75581, 0.56236, 0.51107. stem: A finite, unswept subsonic wing has b=20 m, S=45 m², CL0=0.20 and a0=2pi rad⁻¹ for its sections. Use a=a0/[1+a0/(pi AR)]. At W=104000 N, rho=0.868 kg/m³ and TAS=117 m/s, what angle of attack is needed for level flight, assuming attached linear flow? Choose the closest value.
explanation: AR=b²/S=8.8889, hence the finite-wing slope is a=5.1291 rad⁻¹. Level flight requires CL=0.38901. alpha=(CL−CL0)/a=0.03685 rad=2.1114°. A two-dimensional section slope would underpredict the required angle.

subtopic: Identify two aerodynamic constants from two measurements
stem: A wing is measured at (CL=0.39, xcp/c=0.35302) and (CL=0.78, xcp/c=0.29661). Assume xcp/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL with constant xac and Cm_ac. From the second state, weight falls to 0.882 of its value while rho, V and S stay fixed in level flight. Predict the new xcp/c by first identifying xac and Cm_ac from the two measurements. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Subtract the two pressure-centre equations: Cm_ac=-0.044, then xac/c=0.2402. Constant qS makes CL3=CL2·W3/W2=0.68796. Hence xcp3/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL3=0.30416. The aerodynamic centre does not move with consumed fuel in this model.

option_explanations.0.30416: Correct. Subtract the two pressure-centre equations: Cm_ac=-0.044, then xac/c=0.2402. Constant qS makes CL3=CL2·W3/W2=0.68796. Hence xcp3/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL3=0.30416. The aerodynamic centre does not move with consumed fuel in this model.

option_explanations.0.28995: Inverts the weight ratio when updating CL.

stem: An initially level aircraft has W=121000 N, rho=0.91 kg/m³, S=44 m² and lift-curve slope a=5.22 rad⁻¹. A vertical gust of 8.8 m/s adds delta_alpha≈w_g/V, so CL increases linearly. Require load factor n<= 2.18 and M<=0.65 at T=268 K. Use gamma=1.4 and R=287. What is the highest permitted TAS according to these two limits? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The gust lift increment is delta_L=(rho/2)V S a w_g, not proportional to V² after substituting delta_alpha. Thus V_gust=155.26 m/s. The Mach limit is 213.3 m/s; take their minimum: 155.26 m/s. The resulting load factor is 2.18.

option_explanations.155.26 m/s: Correct. The gust lift increment is delta_L=(rho/2)V S a w_g, not proportional to V² after substituting delta_alpha. Thus V_gust=155.26 m/s. The Mach limit is 213.3 m/s; take their minimum: 155.26 m/s. The resulting load factor is 2.18.

option_explanations.211.03 m/s: Confuses the incremental load factor n−1 with the total n.
option_explanations.558.92 m/s: Converts the correct speed to km/h although m/s is requested.

subtopic: Derive a minimum area from stall
stem: An untwisted trapezoidal wing has fixed b=24 m and root chord=4.6 m. It must carry 210000 N at rho=1.05, achieve Vs<=66 m/s with CLmax=1.85, and require D<=20938 N at Vcr=153 m/s. Use e=0.85, CD0=0.025, S=b cr(1+lambda)/2 and Di=W²/(q pi e b²). Ignoring any additional geometric cap, what is the width lambda_max−lambda_min of the feasible taper-ratio interval? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The stall condition gives Smin=49.636 m². At fixed b, Di=2332.9 N is independent of S in this model; the drag cap gives Smax=(Dmax−Di)/(q CD0)=60.556 m². Convert both through lambda=2S/(b cr)−1: limits -0.10079 and 0.097037, width 0.19783.

stem: A wing of clean area 49 m² and clean CLmax=1.4 must support W=124000 N at rho=0.96 kg/m³. Target approach TAS=61.8 m/s with Vapp>=1.3 Vs. subtopic: Match Mach with temperature-dependent speed of sound
stem: A wind-tunnel model must match BOTH Mach and Reynolds number of an aircraft at M=0.68, T1=253 K, rho1=0.76 kg/m³, chord=2.42 m and mu1=1.6e−5 Pa·s. The model chord is 0.2 times full scale, the tunnel temperature is 303 K and mu2=1.85e−5 Pa·s. For ideal air R=287, gamma=1.4, what tunnel static pressure is required? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Mach matching sets V2/V1=sqrt(T2/T1)=1.0944. Reynolds matching then requires rho2/rho1=(V1/V2)(c1/c2)(mu2/mu1), giving rho2=4.0149 kg/m³. p2=rho2 R T2=349.14 kPa.

explanation: rho=0.68843. Mach sets CL>=0.16305; stall margin sets CL<=0.59763. The unconstrained optimum is 0.72232. Clip it to the feasible CL interval to obtain CL=0.59763; V=sqrt(2W/(rho S CL))=123.66 m/s.

explanation: Transform each test using CL=W/(qS) and CD=D/(qS). Then k=(CD1−CD2)/(CL1²−CL2²)=0.0492, CD0=0.0218. In the new condition CL3=0.42746 and D3=12605 N. Neither measured drag can simply be scaled by V² alone.

stem: At p=67.2 kPa and T=263 K, an aircraft has W=99000 N, S=36 m² and CLmax=1.97. It must fly at V>=1.3 Vs while q<=6900 Pa and M<=0.624. Use R=287 J/(kg K), gamma=1.4. What is the width of the allowable TRUE-airspeed interval? Choose the closest value.
explanation: rho=p/(RT)=0.89029 kg/m³. The lower bound is 1.3 Vs=72.799 m/s. The upper bound is the smaller of the dynamic-pressure and Mach limits: 124.5 m/s. The interval width is (124.5−72.799)×3.6=186.13 km/h.

explanation: The air distances are Dground·TAS/GS. The two log mass ratios are 0.086391 and 0.042555, which ADD: mi=mf exp(k1+k2). With mf=44180 kg, mi=50260 kg. Loaded fuel=mi−OEM−payload=8860.4 kg, including reserve.

explanation: m_dot=75.52 kg/s. Invert the energy equation: T=m_dot[sqrt(V²+2Pjet/m_dot)−V]=7574.4 N. Parasite drag is 5863.8 N; the remainder can cover induced drag. From D=qSCD0+kW²/(qS), Wmax=91425 N.

subtopic: Relate controlled thrust to changing mass
stem: A vertically climbing rocket starts at 3680 kg and must stop burning at 2120 kg. Isp=280 s. Ignore drag; g=g0=9.81 m/s². The controller adjusts thrust continuously to keep NET upward acceleration=5.3 m/s². Using T=m(g+a) and dm/dt=−T/(Isp g0), how long can the burn last? Here thrust is not constant. Choose the closest value.
explanation: The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=100.25 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

subtopic: Identify two aerodynamic constants from two measurements
stem: A wing is measured at (CL=0.4, xcp/c=0.354) and (CL=0.8, xcp/c=0.29775). Assume xcp/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL with constant xac and Cm_ac. From the second state, weight falls to 0.89 of its value while rho, V and S stay fixed in level flight. Predict the new xcp/c by first identifying xac and Cm_ac from the two measurements. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Subtract the two pressure-centre equations: Cm_ac=-0.045, then xac/c=0.2415. Constant qS makes CL3=CL2·W3/W2=0.712. Hence xcp3/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL3=0.3047. The aerodynamic centre does not move with consumed fuel in this model.

stem: An initially level aircraft has W=125000 N, rho=0.92 kg/m³, S=45 m² and lift-curve slope a=5.25 rad⁻¹. A vertical gust of 9 m/s adds delta_alpha≈w_g/V, so CL increases linearly. explanation: The gust lift increment is delta_L=(rho/2)V S a w_g, not proportional to V² after substituting delta_alpha. Thus V_gust=153.36 m/s. The Mach limit is 214.09 m/s; take their minimum: 153.36 m/s. The resulting load factor is 2.2.

stem: A trapezoidal wing has S=45.5 m², b=18.5 m and taper ratio 0.5. It uses ONE four-digit NACA profile throughout the span. Structural depth requires maximum section thickness >= 0.325 m at the root and >= 0.215 m at the tip. Which is the thinnest feasible choice: NACA 2412, 2415, 2418 or 2421?
explanation: Root chord=2S/[b(1+lambda)]=3.2793 m and tip chord=1.6396 m. The required relative thickness is max(0.099107,0.13113)=13.113 %. In this designation the last two digits specify thickness percentage. The smallest feasible candidate is NACA 2415.

subtopic: Match Mach with temperature-dependent speed of sound
stem: A wind-tunnel model must match BOTH Mach and Reynolds number of an aircraft at M=0.68, T1=255 K, rho1=0.775 kg/m³, chord=2.5 m and mu1=1.6e−5 Pa·s. The model chord is 0.205 times full scale, the tunnel temperature is 305 K and mu2=1.85e−5 Pa·s. For ideal air R=287, gamma=1.4, what tunnel static pressure is required? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Mach matching sets V2/V1=sqrt(T2/T1)=1.0937. Reynolds matching then requires rho2/rho1=(V1/V2)(c1/c2)(mu2/mu1), giving rho2=3.9969 kg/m³. p2=rho2 R T2=349.87 kPa.

option_explanations.349.87 kPa: Correct. Mach matching sets V2/V1=sqrt(T2/T1)=1.0937. Reynolds matching then requires rho2/rho1=(V1/V2)(c1/c2)(mu2/mu1), giving rho2=3.9969 kg/m³. p2=rho2 R T2=349.87 kPa.
option_explanations.330.93 kPa: Uses only inverse geometric scaling and ignores the temperature and viscosity corrections.
option_explanations.302.59 kPa: Assumes equal viscosities despite the stated values.
option_explanations.13.907 kPa: Reduces tunnel density with model size instead of increasing it to preserve Reynolds number.

subtopic: Build the feasible CL interval from two speed limits
stem: At p=50 kPa and T=250 K, W=310000 N and S=98 m², a wing follows CD=0.024+0.046CL² with CLmax=1.025. Require TAS>=1.3Vs and M<=0.75. Use R=287 and gamma=1.4. What feasible TAS maximises L/D? Apply the speed limits before accepting the unconstrained polar optimum. Choose the closest value.
explanation: rho=0.69686. Mach sets CL>=0.16067; stall margin sets CL<=0.60651. The unconstrained optimum is 0.72232. Clip it to the feasible CL interval to obtain CL=0.60651; V=sqrt(2W/(rho S CL))=122.35 m/s.

option_explanations.122.35 m/s: Correct. rho=0.69686. Mach sets CL>=0.16067; stall margin sets CL<=0.60651. The unconstrained optimum is 0.72232. Clip it to the feasible CL interval to obtain CL=0.60651; V=sqrt(2W/(rho S CL))=122.35 m/s.
option_explanations.112.11 m/s: Uses the unconstrained optimum even if it violates the approach-to-stall margin.
option_explanations.94.112 m/s: Uses CLmax itself and therefore removes the specified 1.3 speed margin.
option_explanations.237.7 m/s: Selects the maximum Mach speed without optimising efficiency within the admissible range.

stem: Level-flight tests of W=180000 N, S=68 m² at rho=0.9 measure D=12176 N at V=105 m/s and D=18355 N at V=155 m/s. Assume CD=CD0+kCL² with unchanged coefficients. After identifying BOTH coefficients, predict D at rho=0.72 and V=135 m/s for the same W and S. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Transform each test using CL=W/(qS) and CD=D/(qS). Then k=(CD1−CD2)/(CL1²−CL2²)=0.0495, CD0=0.022. In the new condition CL3=0.40345 and D3=13410 N. Neither measured drag can simply be scaled by V² alone.

option_explanations.13410 N: Correct. Transform each test using CL=W/(qS) and CD=D/(qS). Then k=(CD1−CD2)/(CL1²−CL2²)=0.0495, CD0=0.022. In the new condition CL3=0.40345 and D3=13410 N. Neither measured drag can simply be scaled by V² alone.
option_explanations.16102 N: Scales the first total drag as though the induced term had the same V² dependence as parasite drag.
option_explanations.11139 N: Makes the same incorrect total-drag scaling from the second measurement.
option_explanations.9815.3 N: Keeps only the parasite contribution and omits lift-induced drag.

stem: At p=68.5 kPa and T=265 K, an aircraft has W=102500 N, S=37 m² and CLmax=2. It must fly at V>=1.3 Vs while q<=7000 Pa and M<=0.63. Use R=287 J/(kg K), gamma=1.4. What is the width of the allowable TRUE-airspeed interval? Choose the closest value.
explanation: rho=p/(RT)=0.90066 kg/m³. The lower bound is 1.3 Vs=72.098 m/s. The upper bound is the smaller of the dynamic-pressure and Mach limits: 124.68 m/s. The interval width is (124.68−72.098)×3.6=189.28 km/h.

option_explanations.189.28 km/h: Correct. rho=p/(RT)=0.90066 kg/m³. The lower bound is 1.3 Vs=72.098 m/s. The upper bound is the smaller of the dynamic-pressure and Mach limits: 124.68 m/s. The interval width is (124.68−72.098)×3.6=189.28 km/h.

option_explanations.52.578 km/h: Leaves the interval width in m/s although the requested unit is km/h.

stem: An aircraft has W=140000 N, rho=0.9, S=50 m², CLmax=1.7 and CD=0.025+0.052CL². Available USEFUL thrust power is 902.98 kW. Speeds A–D are 66.549, 78.649, 94.73, 118.41 m/s. Which is the LOWEST listed speed satisfying both V>=1.2Vs and D·V<=available power? Do not identify minimum drag with minimum power.

stem: A runway procedure limits groundspeed on approach to 145 km/h with a steady 21 km/h headwind. Require TAS>=1.3 Vs. At p=75.5 kPa and T=286 K, the aircraft has S=36 m², CLmax=2.025 and a structural mass limit of 5200 kg. Use R=287 and g=9.81. What is the greatest mass meeting both the aerodynamic and structural limits? Choose the closest value.
explanation: A headwind means TAS=GS+headwind, so the largest allowed TAS is 46.111 m/s. rho=0.91981; Vs must be <=TAS/1.3. The resulting aerodynamic mass limit is 4299.8 kg. Intersect it with 5200 kg: 4299.8 kg.

option_explanations.4299.8 kg: Correct. A headwind means TAS=GS+headwind, so the largest allowed TAS is 46.111 m/s. rho=0.91981; Vs must be <=TAS/1.3. The resulting aerodynamic mass limit is 4299.8 kg. Intersect it with 5200 kg: 4299.8 kg.

subtopic: Convert each ground distance to distance through the air
stem: A mission has two consecutive cruise legs: 1950 km over ground at TAS=220 m/s into a 27 m/s wind, then 1350 km at TAS=230 m/s with the same tailwind. E1=16.25, ce1=14.6 g/(kN s); E2=16.5, ce2=14 g/(kN s). OEM=29000 kg, payload=13250 kg and final reserve=2850 kg. Use g=9.81, separate ideal Breguet legs and no other fuel use. How much fuel must be loaded at the start? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The air distances are Dground·TAS/GS. The two log mass ratios are 0.089052 and 0.043723, which ADD: mi=mf exp(k1+k2). With mf=45100 kg, mi=51504 kg. Loaded fuel=mi−OEM−payload=9253.9 kg, including reserve.

option_explanations.9253.9 kg: Correct. The air distances are Dground·TAS/GS. The two log mass ratios are 0.089052 and 0.043723, which ADD: mi=mf exp(k1+k2). With mf=45100 kg, mi=51504 kg. Loaded fuel=mi−OEM−payload=9253.9 kg, including reserve.

option_explanations.6403.9 kg: Reports burned fuel only, omitting the required final reserve.

stem: In level flight, groundspeed is 115 m/s with a 16.5 m/s headwind. Ambient p=64.5 kPa, T=270 K; W=145000 N, S=48 m² and CD=0.026+0.052CL². A motor passes 9.5 kg/s and exhausts at 365 m/s; exit static pressure is 78 kPa. Use ideal air R=287 and T=m_dot(Ve−V0)+Ae(pe−pamb). What exit area Ae balances drag? Choose the closest value.
explanation: TAS=GS+headwind=131.5 m/s; rho=0.83237. CL=0.41975, drag=12146 N. Momentum supplies 2218.2 N. The remainder requires Ae=[D−m_dot(Ve−V)]/(pe−pamb)=0.73542 m².

option_explanations.0.73542 m²: Correct. TAS=GS+headwind=131.5 m/s; rho=0.83237. CL=0.41975, drag=12146 N. Momentum supplies 2218.2 N. The remainder requires Ae=[D−m_dot(Ve−V)]/(pe−pamb)=0.73542 m².

stem: An ideal propulsor intercepts m_dot=rho A V, with rho=0.95 kg/m³, A=0.8 m² and V=105 m/s. It transfers 1200 kW of kinetic power to the stream, with no pressure-thrust term. A wing of S=50 m² has CD=0.024+0.05CL². Using Pjet=T·V+T²/(2m_dot) and level flight, what greatest aircraft WEIGHT can its thrust balance? Choose the closest value.
explanation: m_dot=79.8 kg/s. Invert the energy equation: T=m_dot[sqrt(V²+2Pjet/m_dot)−V]=7799 N. Parasite drag is 6284.2 N; the remainder can cover induced drag. From D=qSCD0+kW²/(qS), Wmax=89065 N.

option_explanations.89065 N: Correct. m_dot=79.8 kg/s. Invert the energy equation: T=m_dot[sqrt(V²+2Pjet/m_dot)−V]=7799 N. Parasite drag is 6284.2 N; the remainder can cover induced drag. From D=qSCD0+kW²/(qS), Wmax=89065 N.

option_explanations.1.6413e+05 N: Assumes all kinetic power becomes useful TV, giving an unrealistically large available thrust.
option_explanations.9079 N: Converts the correct weight into mass although the question requests newtons.

subtopic: Relate controlled thrust to changing mass
stem: A vertically climbing rocket starts at 3800 kg and must stop burning at 2200 kg. Isp=285 s. Ignore drag; g=g0=9.81 m/s². The controller adjusts thrust continuously to keep NET upward acceleration=5.5 m/s². Using T=m(g+a) and dm/dt=−T/(Isp g0), how long can the burn last? Here thrust is not constant. Choose the closest value.
explanation: The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=99.808 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

option_explanations.99.808 s: Correct. The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=99.808 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.
option_explanations.76.891 s: Freezes thrust at its initial value and integrates a constant mass flow.
option_explanations.155.76 s: Omits the commanded net acceleration and treats the burn as if T=mg.
option_explanations.277.83 s: Uses net acceleration alone in the thrust law, omitting weight.

stem: An ideal two-stream turbofan has core flow=25 kg/s, V0=190 m/s and core exit speed=435 m/s. Required total thrust is 16000 N and total propulsive efficiency must be at least 0.755. Ignore fuel-added mass and pressure terms. Bypass flow=B·m_core. Use Pjet=sum[m_dot(Vexit²−V0²)/2] and eta=Ttotal V0/Pjet. What minimum bypass ratio B meets the target? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Tcore=6125 N and Tfan=9875 N. Core kinetic power=1914.1 kW. Fan power=V0 Tfan+Tfan²/(2 B m_core). Applying Ptotal<=Ttotal V0/eta leaves 236.18 kW for the last term, so B>=8.2578. This corresponds to fan exit speed 237.83 m/s.

option_explanations.8.2578: Correct. Tcore=6125 N and Tfan=9875 N. Core kinetic power=1914.1 kW. Fan power=V0 Tfan+Tfan²/(2 B m_core). Applying Ptotal<=Ttotal V0/eta leaves 236.18 kW for the last term, so B>=8.2578. This corresponds to fan exit speed 237.83 m/s.

option_explanations.9.2578: Adds the core flow to the numerator, confusing total/core flow ratio with bypass/core ratio.

stem: A propulsor must balance the full drag of a level aircraft at W=127500 N, S=50 m², V=130 m/s, p=73 kPa and T=280 K. CD=0.025+0.05CL². The ideal jet must achieve eta_p>=0.825. With eta_p=2/(1+Ve/V), T=m_dot(Ve−V), m_dot=rho A V and R=287, what minimum intake area A is required? Choose the closest value.

stem: Two ideal jet cruises retain pressure 41800 Pa, Mach 0.748, mean weight 4.16e+05 N, area 110 m², polar CD=0.021+0.046 CL² and mass ratio mi/mf. Temperature changes from 240 to 266 K; ce1=1.46e-05 and ce2=1.5388e-05 kg/(N s). With R=287 J/(kg K) and gamma=1.4, what is Breguet range ratio R2/R1? Determine whether q and L/D change. Choose the closest value.
explanation: At fixed pressure and Mach, q=rho V²/2=gamma p M²/2 is unchanged. Thus CL and L/D are unchanged. Speed ratio is sqrt(T2/T1), so R2/R1=sqrt(T2/T1)×ce1/ce2=0.99884.

stem: An aircraft must maintain V>=1.25Vs at p=74000 Pa, T=274 K, S=56 m² and CLmax=1.78. It must also remain below q=7700 Pa and Mach 0.748. With R=287 J/(kg K), gamma=1.4 and g=9.81 m/s², what maximum mass admits at least one speed satisfying all three conditions? Choose the closest value.
explanation: First rho=p/(RT)=0.94102 kg/m³. Convert both limits to speed: Vq=sqrt(2qmax/rho), VM=Mmax sqrt(gamma RT). Choose their minimum Vcap=127.93 m/s. At the maximum mass, Vs=Vcap/1.25, giving mmax=rho(Vcap/1.25)²S CLmax/(2g)=50074 kg.

subtopic: Calculate CL=0.31994, drag D=9696.2 N and fuel flow ce D.
stem: A round trip has two legs of 2.2e+05 m each at true airspeed 133 m/s. stem: An ideal jet has OEM=27200 kg, MTOM=62600 kg, maximum landing mass=52200 kg, maximum payload=25000 kg and fuel capacity=18600 kg. It must finish with reserve 2300 kg and cover 3.8e+06 m at V=238 m/s, E=16.2, ce=1.46e-05 kg/(N s), g=9.81 m/s². There are no other phases. What maximum payload satisfies every limit, including fuel required by the resulting aircraft mass? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Set k=exp[Rgce/(VE)]=1.1516. Final mass=OEM+payload+reserve and initial mass=k×final mass. Loaded fuel=(k-1)(OEM+payload)+k reserve. Derive payload upper bounds from maximum payload, take-off mass, landing mass and tank capacity; their values are 25000, 24859, 22700, 78013. The minimum is 22700 kg.

subtopic: Identify two aerodynamic constants from two measurements
stem: A wing is measured at (CL=0.41, xcp/c=0.355) and (CL=0.82, xcp/c=0.2989). Assume xcp/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL with constant xac and Cm_ac. stem: A vertically climbing rocket starts at 3920 kg and must stop burning at 2280 kg. Isp=290 s. Ignore drag; g=g0=9.81 m/s². The controller adjusts thrust continuously to keep NET upward acceleration=5.7 m/s². Using T=m(g+a) and dm/dt=−T/(Isp g0), how long can the burn last? Here thrust is not constant. Choose the closest value.
explanation: The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=99.4 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

stem: A vertically climbing rocket starts at 4040 kg and must stop burning at 2360 kg. Isp=295 s. Ignore drag; g=g0=9.81 m/s². explanation: The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=99.029 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

subtopic: Calculate CL=0.29151, drag D=11037 N and fuel flow ce D.
stem: A round trip has two legs of 2.4e+05 m each at true airspeed 139 m/s. Estimate cruise at constant mean weight 1.1e+05 N, rho=0.93 kg/m³, area 42 m², polar CD=0.025+0.05 CL² and ce=1.76e-05 kg/(N s). Available fuel for these two legs is 872.02 kg, with no other phases or reserves. Steady wind is a headwind outbound and tailwind inbound. What maximum wind magnitude w<V meets the fuel budget? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Calculate CL=0.29151, drag D=11037 N and fuel flow ce D. Fuel budget permits tmax=4489.2 s. Since t=d/(V-w)+d/(V+w)=2dV/(V²-w²), solve wmax=sqrt[V²-2dV/tmax]=66.773 m/s.

stem: An ideal jet has OEM=28600 kg, MTOM=65800 kg, maximum landing mass=54600 kg, maximum payload=26000 kg and fuel capacity=19800 kg. It must finish with reserve 2400 kg and cover 4e+06 m at V=244 m/s, E=16.6, ce=1.48e-05 kg/(N s), g=9.81 m/s². There are no other phases. What maximum payload satisfies every limit, including fuel required by the resulting aircraft mass? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Set k=exp[Rgce/(VE)]=1.1542. Final mass=OEM+payload+reserve and initial mass=k×final mass. Loaded fuel=(k-1)(OEM+payload)+k reserve. Derive payload upper bounds from maximum payload, take-off mass, landing mass and tank capacity; their values are 26000, 26011, 23600, 81862. The minimum is 23600 kg.

stem: A vertically climbing rocket starts at 4160 kg and must stop burning at 2440 kg. Isp=300 s. Ignore drag; g=g0=9.81 m/s². The controller adjusts thrust continuously to keep NET upward acceleration=6.1 m/s². Using T=m(g+a) and dm/dt=−T/(Isp g0), how long can the burn last? Here thrust is not constant. Choose the closest value.
explanation: The mass equation is dm/dt=−[(g+a)/(Isp g0)]m. Integrating gives t=Isp g0/(g+a)·ln(mi/mf)=98.689 s. A constant initial thrust would produce a different mass history and would not maintain the stated acceleration.

What CL is needed for level flight? Use gamma=1.4. Choose the closest value.
explanation: The active differential-pressure limit gives ambient p=pc-dpmax=17200 Pa and h=12738 m. Find rho=0.27662 kg/m³ and V=M sqrt(gamma RT)=233.67 m/s. Level flight requires CL=2W/(rho V²S)=0.51099.

subtopic: Pressure inversion gives T_ISA=250.64 K and altitude h=5770 m.
stem: Measured airfield pressure is 48682 Pa and measured temperature is 271.64 K. Pressure follows ISA despite a warm day. Invert p/p0=(T_ISA/288.15)^[9.80665/(0.0065R)], T_ISA=288.15-0.0065h, with p0=101325 Pa and R=287 J/(kg K). An aircraft has weight 59056 N, area 36 m² and CLmax=1.975. Using measured temperature for density and Vapp=1.3Vs, what is true approach speed in km/h? Use g=9.81 m/s² for aircraft weight. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Pressure inversion gives T_ISA=250.64 K and altitude h=5770 m. Actual rho=p/(R T_measured)=0.62443 kg/m³. Then Vs=sqrt[2W/(rho S CLmax)]=51.579 m/s and Vapp=1.3Vs×3.6=241.39 km/h.

option_explanations.241.39 km/h: Correct. Pressure inversion gives T_ISA=250.64 K and altitude h=5770 m. Actual rho=p/(R T_measured)=0.62443 kg/m³. Then Vs=sqrt[2W/(rho S CLmax)]=51.579 m/s and Vapp=1.3Vs×3.6=241.39 km/h.

subtopic: Calculate CL=0.27852, drag D=11768 N and fuel flow ce D.
stem: A round trip has two legs of 2.5e+05 m each at true airspeed 142 m/s. Estimate cruise at constant mean weight 1.135e+05 N, rho=0.94 kg/m³, area 43 m², polar CD=0.025+0.05 CL² and ce=1.78e-05 kg/(N s). Available fuel for these two legs is 969.94 kg, with no other phases or reserves. Steady wind is a headwind outbound and tailwind inbound. What maximum wind magnitude w<V meets the fuel budget? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Calculate CL=0.27852, drag D=11768 N and fuel flow ce D. Fuel budget permits tmax=4630.3 s. Since t=d/(V-w)+d/(V+w)=2dV/(V²-w²), solve wmax=sqrt[V²-2dV/tmax]=69.499 m/s.

option_explanations.34.015 m/s: Uses a linear headwind correction instead of adding both leg times.
option_explanations.250.2 m/s: Converts the result to km/h while retaining the m/s label.
option_explanations.69.499 m/s: Correct. Calculate CL=0.27852, drag D=11768 N and fuel flow ce D. Fuel budget permits tmax=4630.3 s. Since t=d/(V-w)+d/(V+w)=2dV/(V²-w²), solve wmax=sqrt[V²-2dV/tmax]=69.499 m/s.

stem: An ideal jet has OEM=29300 kg, MTOM=67400 kg, maximum landing mass=55800 kg, maximum payload=26500 kg and fuel capacity=20400 kg. It must finish with reserve 2450 kg and cover 4.1e+06 m at V=247 m/s, E=16.8, ce=1.49e-05 kg/(N s), g=9.81 m/s². There are no other phases. What maximum payload satisfies every limit, including fuel required by the resulting aircraft mass? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Set k=exp[Rgce/(VE)]=1.1554. Final mass=OEM+payload+reserve and initial mass=k×final mass. Loaded fuel=(k-1)(OEM+payload)+k reserve. Derive payload upper bounds from maximum payload, take-off mass, landing mass and tank capacity; their values are 26500, 26586, 24050, 83780. The minimum is 24050 kg.

explanation: Take-off mass=min(MTOM,OEM+payload+tank capacity)=66050 kg. Cruise initial mass=63620 kg after prior burn; final mass=OEM+payload+reserve=50290 kg. Apply R=VE ln(mi/mf)/(g ce)=7.0038e+06 m and convert to km.

explanation: Convert B test flow to kg/s and divide by test thrust in N: ceB=1.2915e-05 kg/(N s). Mission fuel-flow ratio=(ceB/(ceA×10^-6))×mission thrust ratio=0.79859. Percentage change=100(ratio-1)=-20.141%. Test thrust establishes ceB; mission thrust determines mission flow.

stem: Compare four rectangular cantilevers under F=410 N, L=1.325 m, E=70 GPa: A 35×45 mm; B 45×50 mm; C 35×60 mm; D 50×55 mm (width×height). stem: A finite, unswept subsonic wing has b=22.5 m, S=52.5 m², CL0=0.20 and a0=2pi rad⁻¹ for its sections. Use a=a0/[1+a0/(pi AR)]. At W=119000 N, rho=0.928 kg/m³ and TAS=132 m/s, what angle of attack is needed for level flight, assuming attached linear flow? Choose the closest value.

subtopic: Identify two aerodynamic constants from two measurements
stem: A wing is measured at (CL=0.44, xcp/c=0.35806) and (CL=0.88, xcp/c=0.30238). Assume xcp/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL with constant xac and Cm_ac. From the second state, weight falls to 0.922 of its value while rho, V and S stay fixed in level flight. Predict the new xcp/c by first identifying xac and Cm_ac from the two measurements. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Subtract the two pressure-centre equations: Cm_ac=-0.049, then xac/c=0.2467. Constant qS makes CL3=CL2·W3/W2=0.81136. Hence xcp3/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL3=0.30709. The aerodynamic centre does not move with consumed fuel in this model.

option_explanations.0.30709: Correct. Subtract the two pressure-centre equations: Cm_ac=-0.049, then xac/c=0.2467. Constant qS makes CL3=CL2·W3/W2=0.81136. Hence xcp3/c=xac/c−Cm_ac/CL3=0.30709. The aerodynamic centre does not move with consumed fuel in this model.

subtopic: Find Vmd as the speed scale
stem: A jet aircraft has W=391000 N, rho=0.6, S=113 m² and CD=0.022+0.045CL². Four cruise TAS candidates A–D are [1.00,1.12,1.28,1.48] times Vmd. stem: An initially level aircraft has W=141000 N, rho=0.96 kg/m³, S=49 m² and lift-curve slope a=5.37 rad⁻¹. A vertical gust of 9.8 m/s adds delta_alpha≈w_g/V, so CL increases linearly. Require load factor n<= 2.28 and M<=0.65 at T=278 K. Use gamma=1.4 and R=287. What is the highest permitted TAS according to these two limits? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The gust lift increment is delta_L=(rho/2)V S a w_g, not proportional to V² after substituting delta_alpha. Thus V_gust=145.81 m/s. The Mach limit is 217.24 m/s; take their minimum: 145.81 m/s. The resulting load factor is 2.28.

option_explanations.145.81 m/s: Correct. The gust lift increment is delta_L=(rho/2)V S a w_g, not proportional to V² after substituting delta_alpha. Thus V_gust=145.81 m/s. The Mach limit is 217.24 m/s; take their minimum: 145.81 m/s. The resulting load factor is 2.28.
option_explanations.217.24 m/s: Uses the looser rather than the tighter of two simultaneous limits.
option_explanations.194.6 m/s: Confuses the incremental load factor n−1 with the total n.
option_explanations.524.92 m/s: Converts the correct speed to km/h although m/s is requested.

stem: An untwisted trapezoidal wing has fixed b=26.5 m and root chord=5.1 m. It must carry 235000 N at rho=1.05, achieve Vs<=71 m/s with CLmax=1.85, and require D<=23368 N at Vcr=163 m/s. Use e=0.85, CD0=0.025, S=b cr(1+lambda)/2 and Di=W²/(q pi e b²). Ignoring any additional geometric cap, what is the width lambda_max−lambda_min of the feasible taper-ratio interval? explanation: The stall condition gives Smin=47.998 m². At fixed b, Di=2111.3 N is independent of S in this model; the drag cap gives Smax=(Dmax−Di)/(q CD0)=60.957 m². Convert both through lambda=2S/(b cr)−1: limits -0.28971 and -0.097935, width 0.19178.

stem: A wing of clean area 54 m² and clean CLmax=1.4 must support W=141500 N at rho=1.01 kg/m³. Target approach TAS=67.8 m/s with Vapp>=1.3 Vs. Deploying a Fowler system increases area by a factor 1.17. CLmax in each configuration uses its OWN area. What minimum factor CLmax_deployed/CLmax_clean is needed? Choose the closest value.
explanation: The allowed stall speed is Vapp/1.3=52.154 m/s. With deployed S=63.18 m², CLmax_required=2W/[rho (Vapp/1.3)² S_deployed]=1.6305. Relative to the clean coefficient, the gain must be 1.1646.

stem: A trapezoidal wing has S=51.5 m², b=20.5 m and taper ratio 0.54. It uses ONE four-digit NACA profile throughout the span. Structural depth requires maximum section thickness >= 0.353 m at the root and >= 0.235 m at the tip. Which is the thinnest feasible choice: NACA 2412, 2415, 2418 or 2421?
explanation: Root chord=2S/[b(1+lambda)]=3.2626 m and tip chord=1.7618 m. The required relative thickness is max(0.1082,0.13339)=13.339 %. In this designation the last two digits specify thickness percentage. The smallest feasible candidate is NACA 2415.

stem: A wind-tunnel model must match BOTH Mach and Reynolds number of an aircraft at M=0.68, T1=263 K, rho1=0.835 kg/m³, chord=2.82 m and mu1=1.6e−5 Pa·s. The model chord is 0.225 times full scale, the tunnel temperature is 313 K and mu2=1.85e−5 Pa·s. For ideal air R=287, gamma=1.4, what tunnel static pressure is required? Choose the closest value.
explanation: Mach matching sets V2/V1=sqrt(T2/T1)=1.0909. Reynolds matching then requires rho2/rho1=(V1/V2)(c1/c2)(mu2/mu1), giving rho2=3.9333 kg/m³. p2=rho2 R T2=353.34 kPa.

stem: At p=54 kPa and T=258 K, W=342000 N and S=106 m², a wing follows CD=0.024+0.046CL² with CLmax=1.085. Require TAS>=1.3Vs and M<=0.75. Use R=287 and gamma=1.4. What feasible TAS maximises L/D? Apply the speed limits before accepting the unconstrained polar optimum. Choose the closest value.
explanation: rho=0.72928. Mach sets CL>=0.15174; stall margin sets CL<=0.64201. The unconstrained optimum is 0.72232. Clip it to the feasible CL interval to obtain CL=0.64201; V=sqrt(2W/(rho S CL))=117.4 m/s.

option_explanations.117.4 m/s: Correct. rho=0.72928. Mach sets CL>=0.15174; stall margin sets CL<=0.64201. The unconstrained optimum is 0.72232. Clip it to the feasible CL interval to obtain CL=0.64201; V=sqrt(2W/(rho S CL))=117.4 m/s.
option_explanations.110.68 m/s: Uses the unconstrained optimum even if it violates the approach-to-stall margin.
option_explanations.90.305 m/s: Uses CLmax itself and therefore removes the specified 1.3 speed margin.
option_explanations.241.48 m/s: Selects the maximum Mach speed without optimising efficiency within the admissible range.

stem: Level-flight tests of W=200000 N, S=76 m² at rho=0.94 measure D=14846 N at V=113 m/s and D=23775 N at V=163 m/s. Assume CD=CD0+kCL² with unchanged coefficients. After identifying BOTH coefficients, predict D at rho=0.752 and V=147 m/s for the same W and S. Choose the closest value.
explanation: Transform each test using CL=W/(qS) and CD=D/(qS). Then k=(CD1−CD2)/(CL1²−CL2²)=0.0507, CD0=0.0228. In the new condition CL3=0.32389 and D3=17363 N. Neither measured drag can simply be scaled by V² alone.

option_explanations.17363 N: Correct. Transform each test using CL=W/(qS) and CD=D/(qS). Then k=(CD1−CD2)/(CL1²−CL2²)=0.0507, CD0=0.0228. In the new condition CL3=0.32389 and D3=17363 N. Neither measured drag can simply be scaled by V² alone.
option_explanations.20099 N: Scales the first total drag as though the induced term had the same V² dependence as parasite drag.
option_explanations.15469 N: Makes the same incorrect total-drag scaling from the second measurement.
option_explanations.14079 N: Keeps only the parasite contribution and omits lift-induced drag.
